raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t chase fancy things. On my 2.6 mu, I’ll still plant cotton like I’ve done for years. Cotton suits this land, and with such a small plot I know every corner of it. I only finished primary school, so I don’t talk in big technical terms. I look at what worked before, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash we can spare. Last year if the stand was decent with moderate fertilizer, I’ll stay close to that. I have a well, so if spring is dry I’m not too afraid, but water costs money, so I won’t irrigate too many times unless the crop really needs it. I’d rather spend carefully and keep the field steady than gamble on spending a lot for a maybe.

For seed, I’ll buy local improved cotton seed if the price is reasonable, because saved seed is not as reliable for yield. I’ll sow around mid to late April, after the ground warms up. Before planting I’ll put on some base fertilizer, not too much, then give another topdressing later if the cotton is growing weak. I’ll do normal tillage with a small machine or hired help if needed, because cotton likes a clean seedbed. Weed and insect problems come most years, so I’ll plan for herbicide and some insecticide, but I won’t spray unless I see the need. Labor is mostly from the two of us at home, and for picking we may need a little extra help if the bolls open all at once.
